subproblems.title: Compatible compactly supported pull-backs exist (cut-off of Simon 2.23)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), IsOpen U → A ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ A)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn V j, ∃ (η : TestFormOn U j) (ζ : Eucl P → ℝ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen N ∧ A ⊆ N ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ζ x ∧ ζ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ζ x • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∧ tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) ⊆ f ⁻¹' tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 4–6 of the parent proof. Those steps build a smooth Urysohn cut-off ζ ≡ 1 near the compact set K′ = p⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ {d ≤ γ}, form the test form η := ζ·p^#ω, and show that η agrees with p^#ω on an open set containing spt Z_k. This is the cut-off of the printed definition 2.23 of Simon Ch. 6: f_#T(ω) = T(ζ f^#ω), where ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U) is identically one in a neighbourhood of the compact set spt T ∩ spt f^#ω. In this child, the linear map p is replaced by a C^∞ map f, and spt Z_k by an arbitrary set A ⊆ U on which f is proper. Smoothness of the pull-back is therefore proved for a non-constant derivative Df (step 4).

Notation: g(x) := (f^#ω)(x) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x). “C^∞” means ContDiff of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞).

1. (The compact set.) Since ω ∈ D^j(V) = TestFormOn V j, ω is C^∞, has compact support, and tsupport ω ⊆ V. So tsupport ω is a compact subset of V (HasCompactSupport.isCompact). By the properness hypothesis, K′ := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A is compact, and K′ ⊆ A ⊆ U.

2. (Thickenings.) K′ is compact, U is open and K′ ⊆ U, so there is δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K′ ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Define:
   - O := thickening (δ₀/2) K′, open, with K′ ⊆ O (self_subset_thickening, as δ₀/2 > 0);
   - C := cthickening (δ₀/2) K′, closed, with O ⊆ C (thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - s := thickening δ₀ K′, open, with C ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ₀ and δ₀/2 < δ₀).
   If K′ = ∅, all three sets are empty and the argument below still applies.

3. (The cut-off.) Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (order ⊤) to the open set s and the closed set C ⊆ s. It gives a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = s, and ζ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ C. Consequently:
   - 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1 for every x, and ζ = 1 on O ⊆ C;
   - tsupport ζ = closure s ⊆ cthickening δ₀ K′ ⊆ U (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - cthickening δ₀ K′ is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so its closed subset tsupport ζ is compact, i.e. ζ has compact support.

4. (g is C^∞.)
   (a) x ↦ fderiv ℝ f x is C^∞ because f is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right, using ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞, where ∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)).
   (b) x ↦ ω(f(x)) is C^∞, as the composition of the C^∞ maps ω and f (ContDiff.comp).
   (c) Consider the map B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B. It sends a continuous linear map B : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap B on j-covectors. It is analytic on the whole space (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).
   (d) g(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (fderiv ℝ f x)) (ω(f x)), so g is C^∞ by ContDiff.comp and ContDiff.clm_apply.

5. (The test form.) Define η(x) := ζ(x) • g(x).
   - η is C^∞ by ContDiff.smul, using steps 3 and 4.
   - tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Hence η has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport η ⊆ U by step 3.
   Therefore η ∈ D^j(U) = TestFormOn U j, and η(x) = ζ(x) • g(x) for every x by definition.

6. (Support.) Suppose f(x) ∉ tsupport ω. Then ω(f(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). The pull-back of the zero covector is zero, so g(x) = 0 and η(x) = 0. Hence support η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω). This set is closed, because f is continuous and tsupport ω is closed. So tsupport η = closure(support η) ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) (closure_minimal).

7. (The open set N.) Put N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω).
   - N is open: O is open, and f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω) is the preimage of an open set under the continuous map f.
   - A ⊆ N: let x ∈ A. If f(x) ∈ tsupport ω, then x ∈ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A = K′ ⊆ O. Otherwise x ∈ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω).

8. (η = g on N.) Let x ∈ N.
   - If x ∈ O, then x ∈ C, so ζ(x) = 1 and η(x) = g(x).
   - If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then η(x) = 0 = g(x) by step 6.

9. (Conclusion.) η ∈ D^j(U), ζ and N have all the required properties:
   - N is open and A ⊆ N (step 7);
   - 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 (step 3);
   - η(x) = ζ(x)·(f^#ω)(x) for all x (step 5);
   - η(x) = (f^#ω)(x) for all x ∈ N (step 8);
   - tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) (step 6). ∎
proof_key_steps: Properness makes K′ := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A a compact subset of the open set U.
Choose δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K′ ⊆ U. Smooth Urysohn on thickenings of K′ gives a C^∞ cut-off ζ with values in [0, 1], compact support in U, and ζ = 1 on O := thickening (δ₀/2) K′.
The pull-back g = f^#ω is C^∞: Df is C^∞, and B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B is analytic. So η := ζ·g ∈ D^j(U).
η vanishes where f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, so tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω).
η = g on the open set N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), which contains A.

subproblems.lean_statement: LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity → (LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity → ∀ (P Q k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)), IsOpen U → IsOpen V → ∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), IsIntegerMultiplicity X → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → MapsTo f U V → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ X.support)) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn V (k + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity S ∧ (∀ (ω : TestFormOn V (k + 1)) (η : TestFormOn U (k + 1)), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (k + 1)) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) (k + 1)) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S ω = X η) ∧ (∀ (ω : TestFormOn V k) (η : TestFormOn U k), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) k) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S.boundary ω = X.boundary η) ∧ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c → (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ c) → ∀ W : Set (Eucl Q), S.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ (k + 1)) * X.massOn (f ⁻¹' W ∩ U) ∧ S.boundary.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ k) * X.boundary.massOn (f ⁻¹' W ∩ U)) → ∀ (P Q m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (F : Set (Eucl P)) (p : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → IsOpen V → ‖p‖ ≤ 1 → MapsTo p U V → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IsCompact (p ⁻¹' K ∩ F) ∧ p ⁻¹' K ∩ F ⊆ U) → (∀ k, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X k)) → (∀ k, (X k).support ⊆ F) → ∃ S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn V (m + 1), (∀ k, IsIntegerMultiplicity (S k)) ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn V (m + 1)) (η : TestFormOn U (m + 1)), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ (X k).support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) (m + 1)) (p x)).compContinuousLinearMap p) → S k ω = X k η) ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ) (W : Set (Eucl Q)), (S k).massOn W ≤ (X k).mass ∧ (S k).boundary.massOn W ≤ (X k).boundary.mass
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 0–2 of the parent proof, specifically step 0 (p is C^∞ with fderiv ℝ p x = p), step 1 (properness), and step 2(a)–(b) (push-forward by (SPF), and the per-k mass bound from its c = 1 clause). The supremum over k of step 3, which uses sup_k (M(Z_k) + M(∂Z_k)) < ∞, stays in the parent. These steps formalize the printed Proof of 8.2 of Simon Ch. 6, from “p_#S̃_j ∈ D_n(B_1ⁿ(0))” through the mass identities (10). Here the geometric input of the parent (frame_geometry for W′, B_1ⁿ(0) and {d ≤ γ}) is replaced by the hypotheses:
   - U, V are open;
   - ‖p‖ ≤ 1 and p(U) ⊆ V;
   - p⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact and contained in U for every compact K ⊆ V;
   - spt X_k ⊆ F.

1. (p is C^∞ with derivative p.) p is continuous linear, so it is C^∞ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff), and fderiv ℝ p x = p for every x (ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv). Hence ‖fderiv ℝ p x‖ = ‖p‖ ≤ 1 for every x.

2. (Properness of p on spt X_k.) Fix k and a compact K ⊆ V. By hypothesis K′ := p⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact and K′ ⊆ U. Write Z_k := zeroRegion(X_k). It is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), and spt X_k = U ∖ Z_k by definition. We claim p⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X_k = K′ ∖ Z_k.
   - “⊆”: if y ∈ p⁻¹(K) and y ∈ spt X_k, then y ∈ F (since spt X_k ⊆ F) and y ∉ Z_k. So y ∈ K′ ∖ Z_k.
   - “⊇”: if y ∈ K′ and y ∉ Z_k, then y ∈ U (since K′ ⊆ U). Hence y ∈ U ∖ Z_k = spt X_k, and y ∈ p⁻¹(K).
   K′ is compact and Z_k is open, so K′ ∖ Z_k is compact (IsCompact.diff). Therefore p⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X_k is compact for every compact K ⊆ V.

3. (Application of (SPF).) Fix k. Apply (SPF), with the hypothesis LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity, to: P, Q; the degree index m (so X_k ∈ D_{m+1}(U)); the open sets U, V; X := X_k, which is integer multiplicity; and f := p. The hypotheses of (SPF) hold: p is C^∞ (step 1), p(U) ⊆ V, and p⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X_k is compact for every compact K ⊆ V (step 2). (SPF) yields S ∈ D_{m+1}(V) which is integer multiplicity and satisfies:
   (a) S(ω) = X_k(η) whenever ω ∈ D^{m+1}(V), η ∈ D^{m+1}(U), and η(x) = (ω(p x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ p x) for all x in some open N ⊇ spt X_k;
   (b) a boundary identity, which is not needed here;
   (c) for every real c ≥ 0 with ‖fderiv ℝ p x‖ ≤ c for all x, and every W ⊆ ℝ^Q:
       M_W(S) ≤ ofReal(c^{m+1}) · M_{p⁻¹(W) ∩ U}(X_k) and M_W(∂S) ≤ ofReal(c^m) · M_{p⁻¹(W) ∩ U}(∂X_k).
   By the axiom of choice (Lean: choose), pick such an S =: S_k for every k ∈ ℕ. Each S_k is integer multiplicity.

4. (Action identity (i).) Let k, ω ∈ D^{m+1}(V) and η ∈ D^{m+1}(U) be given. Let N be open with spt X_k ⊆ N and η(x) = (ω(p x)).compContinuousLinearMap p for all x ∈ N. Since fderiv ℝ p x = p (step 1), η(x) = (ω(p x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ p x) for all x ∈ N. So 3(a) gives S_k(ω) = X_k(η).

5. (Mass bounds (ii).) Fix k and W ⊆ ℝ^Q. Apply 3(c) with c := 1; this is allowed since 0 ≤ 1 and ‖fderiv ℝ p x‖ ≤ 1 for all x (step 1).
   - Since 1^{m+1} = 1^m = 1, ofReal 1 = 1 and 1·a = a, we get M_W(S_k) ≤ M_{p⁻¹(W) ∩ U}(X_k) and M_W(∂S_k) ≤ M_{p⁻¹(W) ∩ U}(∂X_k).
   - Local mass is monotone in the region (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono), and p⁻¹(W) ∩ U ⊆ U. Hence M_{p⁻¹(W) ∩ U}(X_k) ≤ M_U(X_k) = M(X_k), and likewise M_{p⁻¹(W) ∩ U}(∂X_k) ≤ M_U(∂X_k) = M(∂X_k). (GeometricCurrentOn.mass T is by definition T.massOn U, for X_k and for ∂X_k ∈ D_m(U).)
   - Combining: M_W(S_k) ≤ M(X_k) and M_W(∂S_k) ≤ M(∂X_k).

6. (Conclusion.) The sequence S = (S_k)_{k∈ℕ} consists of integer multiplicity currents in D_{m+1}(V) (step 3) and satisfies (i) (step 4) and (ii) (step 5). ∎
proof_key_steps: p is C^∞ with fderiv ℝ p x = p, hence ‖fderiv ℝ p x‖ ≤ 1.
Properness: p⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X_k = (p⁻¹(K) ∩ F) ∖ zeroRegion(X_k), which is compact since p⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact and contained in U.
Apply (SPF) with f := p for every k and choose S_k: integer multiplicity, with S_k(ω) = X_k(η) whenever η = p^#ω near spt X_k (using fderiv ℝ p = p).
The mass clause of (SPF) at c = 1, with massOn_mono, gives M_W(S_k) ≤ M(X_k) and M_W(∂S_k) ≤ M(∂X_k).
